doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Healing quality of music and stage nerves
summary: Berry says music relieves illness; Cooper keeps his pre-gig nerves; Ella Fitzgerald was scared every night.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: And the other thing that I wanted to ask the two of you, you know, owing to your experience and participation in the Statesmen is, do you think the music itself has a healing quality in it that can get rid of some of this?

Absolutely. No question about it. In fact it has healing qualities in many ways, you can ask any musician, you know you’ve got a fever or upset stomach or a cold or anything like that, but you’ve got to go to work, right? You finish playing and you feel, you know, your headache’s gone, your cold feels like you’re not sick anymore. You are of course, but it relieves all of that, it really does. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

And I’ll tell you another thing too I mean, and I’ll question if he feels the same way, as long as I’ve been playing and in all the places that I have played, I mean all the big places, like he said at the White House and things like that and things for kings and queens. And I got a job in my hometown now because I live in Florida now you know. And I get the queasy stomach, I get nervous before I go to the job. I still get that feeling. But I want to keep that you know, I want to keep that feeling. Because anytime I get that feeling I say I’m not missing anything.
Well of all people, like the greatest, Ella Fitzgerald, was absolutely scared to death every night she had to go on the stage. Scared to death. And she was the best.
